authors: He, Y.; Bárdossy, A.; Zehe, E.
title: A review of regionalisation for continuous streamflow simulation
hydrological_context: Ungauged catchments; continuous discharge
method: Distance-based and regression-based regionalisation
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Continuous streamflow can be estimated by transferring information from gauged catchments through several regionalisation approaches.
claim_supported: Continuous streamflow can be estimated by transferring information from gauged catchments through several regionalisation approaches.
how_we_should_use_it: P1 importance and P2 regionalisation taxonomy.
limitations_or_caution: Review of available approaches; no universal transferability guarantee or local DSK provenance evidence.

authors: Parajka, J.; Viglione, A.; Rogger, M.; Salinas, J. L.; Sivapalan, M.; Blöschl, G.
title: Comparative assessment of predictions in ungauged basins – Part 1: Runoff-hydrograph studies
hydrological_context: Ungauged catchments across climate and landscape settings
method: Meta-analysis and leave-one-out assessment
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Runoff-hydrograph prediction performance varies with climate, catchment properties and regionalisation approach.
claim_supported: Runoff-hydrograph prediction performance varies with climate, catchment properties and regionalisation approach.
how_we_should_use_it: P1 PUB problem; P2 fair discussion of context-dependent regionalisation.
limitations_or_caution: Basin holdout differs from chronological holdout; does not establish our reconstruction mechanism.

authors: Salinas, J. L.; Laaha, G.; Rogger, M.; Parajka, J.; Viglione, A.; Sivapalan, M.; Blöschl, G.
title: Comparative assessment of predictions in ungauged basins – Part 2: Flood and low flow studies
hydrological_context: Ungauged flood and low-flow prediction
method: Meta-analysis and leave-one-out assessment
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Flood and low-flow regionalisation skill depends on climate and catchment characteristics.
claim_supported: Flood and low-flow regionalisation skill depends on climate and catchment characteristics.
how_we_should_use_it: P1 observational limitations and P2 regionalisation scope.
limitations_or_caution: Extreme-flow signatures are distinct from daily reconstruction; do not transfer numerical rankings.

authors: Arsenault, Richard; Martel, Jean-Luc; Brunet, Frédéric; Brissette, François; Mai, Juliane
title: Continuous streamflow prediction in ungauged basins: long short-term memory neural networks clearly outperform traditional hydrological models
hydrological_context: Pseudo-ungauged catchments in northeast North America
method: LSTM versus conceptual-model regionalisation
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: A shared-data comparison found LSTM regionalisation more accurate than the tested conceptual approaches across most study catchments.
claim_supported: A shared-data comparison found LSTM regionalisation more accurate than the tested conceptual approaches across most study catchments.
how_we_should_use_it: P1 information transfer; P2 acknowledge ML strengths.
limitations_or_caution: Regional sample and tested models bound the comparison; title must not become a universal superiority claim.

authors: Kratzert, Frederik; Klotz, Daniel; Brenner, Claire; Schulz, Karsten; Herrnegger, Mathew
title: Rainfall–runoff modelling using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks
hydrological_context: CAMELS rainfall-runoff catchments
method: Local and regional LSTM; SAC-SMA plus Snow-17 comparison
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: LSTM models can learn long-term input-output dependencies and benefit from regional training in the tested rainfall-runoff setting.
claim_supported: LSTM models can learn long-term input-output dependencies and benefit from regional training in the tested rainfall-runoff setting.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 sequence-learning family and temporal storage representation.
limitations_or_caution: Prediction skill is not causal identification; not a river-network routing test.

authors: Kratzert, Frederik; Klotz, Daniel; Shalev, Guy; Klambauer, Günter; Hochreiter, Sepp; Nearing, Grey
title: Towards learning universal, regional, and local hydrological behaviors via machine learning applied to large-sample datasets
hydrological_context: CAMELS multi-basin rainfall-runoff
method: Entity-Aware LSTM with meteorology and static attributes
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: A regional LSTM and its entity-aware variant learn catchment similarities and outperform the evaluated hydrological benchmarks.
claim_supported: A regional LSTM and its entity-aware variant learn catchment similarities and outperform the evaluated hydrological benchmarks.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 multi-basin sequence models; acknowledge analysis of learned catchment representations.
limitations_or_caution: Counterexample to blanket claims that ML ignores hydrological interpretation; not proof of local residual causes.

authors: Gauch, Martin; Kratzert, Frederik; Klotz, Daniel; Nearing, Grey; Lin, Jimmy; Hochreiter, Sepp
title: Rainfall–runoff prediction at multiple timescales with a single Long Short-Term Memory network
hydrological_context: Daily and hourly streamflow prediction in US basins
method: Multi-timescale LSTM
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Joint modelling of multiple temporal resolutions improves computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy against separate LSTM models in the evaluated benchmark.
claim_supported: Joint modelling of multiple temporal resolutions improves computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy against separate LSTM models in the evaluated benchmark.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 timescale-aware ML and distinction between daily envelopes and short peaks.
limitations_or_caution: Not a Transformer study or an independent causal attribution method.

authors: Sun, Alexander Y.; Jiang, Peishi; Yang, Zong-Liang; Xie, Yangxinyu; Chen, Xingyuan
title: A graph neural network (GNN) approach to basin-scale river network learning: the role of physics-based connectivity and data fusion
hydrological_context: US river networks; snow-dominated watershed and larger basin
method: GNN surrogate, observation fine-tuning, graph data fusion and coarsening
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Graph connectivity and data fusion allow river-model emulation and reduction of observation mismatch.
claim_supported: Graph connectivity and data fusion allow river-model emulation and reduction of observation mismatch.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 graph learning; P3 acknowledge existing physics-guided and bias-diagnostic work.
limitations_or_caution: Simulation-trained surrogate skill differs from observation skill; data fusion requires accessible gauges and proper withholding.

authors: Mosaffa, Hamidreza; Pappenberger, Florian; Prudhomme, Christel; Chantry, Matthew; Rüdiger, Christoph; Cloke, Hannah
title: A GNN routing module is all you need for LSTM Rainfall–Runoff models
hydrological_context: Upper Danube; connected subbasins
method: LSTM local runoff generation plus GNN routing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Explicit graph routing improves tested LSTM predictions, particularly at strongly connected downstream locations.
claim_supported: Explicit graph routing improves tested LSTM predictions, particularly at strongly connected downstream locations.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 recent graph routing; P3 acknowledge routing can matter.
limitations_or_caution: One network and evaluated architectures; neither establishes routing failure here nor universal GNN superiority.

authors: Yu, Qiutong; Tolson, Bryan A.; Shen, Hongren; Han, Ming; Mai, Juliane; Lin, Jimmy
title: Enhancing long short-term memory (LSTM)-based streamflow prediction with a spatially distributed approach
hydrological_context: Great Lakes gauged and pseudo-ungauged basins
method: Subbasin LSTM predictions plus physics-based routing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Spatially recursive routing of local LSTM predictions improves prediction in large and pseudo-ungauged basins relative to the tested lumped baseline.
claim_supported: Spatially recursive routing of local LSTM predictions improves prediction in large and pseudo-ungauged basins relative to the tested lumped baseline.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 hybrid methods; P3 distinguish local runoff generation from transport.
limitations_or_caution: Spatial improvement is context dependent; study already distinguishes spatial aggregation and routing.

authors: Mizukami, Naoki; Clark, Martyn P.; Sampson, Kevin; Nijssen, Bart; Mao, Yixin; McMillan, Hilary; Viger, Roland J.; Markstrom, Steve L.; Hay, Lauren E.; Woods, Ross; Arnold, Jeffrey R.; Brekke, Levi D.
title: mizuRoute version 1: a river network routing tool for a continental domain water resources applications
hydrological_context: Headwaters to continental river networks
method: Hillslope unit hydrograph plus channel KWT or IRF-UH routing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Runoff generation and channel transport can be represented in separate stages to estimate discharge along a river network.
claim_supported: Runoff generation and channel transport can be represented in separate stages to estimate discharge along a river network.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 process-based methods; P3 transport cannot substitute for absent local runoff inputs.
limitations_or_caution: Separation is a structural modelling principle, not a diagnosis of the BYBLK-DSK reach.

authors: Colleoni, François; Huynh, Ngo Nghi Truyen; Garambois, Pierre-André; Jay-Allemand, Maxime; Organde, Didier; Renard, Benjamin; De Fournas, Thomas; El Baz, Apolline; Demargne, Julie; Javelle, Pierre
title: smash v1.0: a differentiable and regionalizable high-resolution hydrological modeling and data assimilation framework
hydrological_context: Catchment to regional high-resolution hydrology
method: Modular vertical/lateral processes; adjoint optimisation; linear-reservoir and kinematic-wave routing options
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: A differentiable process-based framework supports local runoff operators, river routing and distributed or regionalised parameter estimation.
claim_supported: A differentiable process-based framework supports local runoff operators, river routing and distributed or regionalised parameter estimation.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 physics-data methods; P3 distinguish routing operator from production operator.
limitations_or_caution: Distributed differentiation is established prior work; our simple routing chain is not equivalent to this framework.
evidence_location: Abstract; routing operator description (linear reservoir module)

authors: Grogan, Danielle S.; Zuidema, Shan; Prusevich, Alex; Wollheim, Wilfred M.; Glidden, Stanley; Lammers, Richard B.
title: Water balance model (WBM) v.1.0.0: a scalable gridded global hydrologic model with water-tracking functionality
hydrological_context: Gridded water cycle, river discharge and irrigation
method: Process-based WBM with Muskingum-Cunge or linear-reservoir routing and water-source tracking
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Routing choice is scale sensitive, and source tracking can distinguish runoff origins and anthropogenic return flows.
claim_supported: Routing choice is scale sensitive, and source tracking can distinguish runoff origins and anthropogenic return flows.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 routing alternatives; P3/D support spatially generated and returned-water contributions.
limitations_or_caution: Global gridded implementation does not validate our residence time, topology or reach-specific processes.

authors: Nguyen-Quang, Trung; Polcher, Jan; Ducharne, Agnès; Arsouze, Thomas; Zhou, Xudong; Schneider, Ana; Fita, Lluís
title: ORCHIDEE-ROUTING: revising the river routing scheme using a high-resolution hydrological database
hydrological_context: Mediterranean rivers across climate and size gradients
method: High-resolution HydroSHEDS-based ORCHIDEE routing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Revised routing captures seasonal discharge variability while substantial biases can still arise from the simulated water budget.
claim_supported: Revised routing captures seasonal discharge variability while substantial biases can still arise from the simulated water budget.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 direct support for separating routing representation errors from runoff/water-budget errors.
limitations_or_caution: Routing improvements were useful in this study; cannot cite as evidence that heterogeneity never helps.

authors: Jay-Allemand, Maxime; Javelle, Pierre; Gejadze, Igor; Arnaud, Patrick; Malaterre, Pierre-Olivier; Fine, Jean-Alain; Organde, Didier
title: On the potential of variational calibration for a fully distributed hydrological model: application on a Mediterranean catchment
hydrological_context: Mediterranean flash-flood catchment
method: Adjoint-based variational calibration of distributed GRD
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Distributed calibration can improve predictions; adequacy, identifiability and numerical stability remain relevant constraints.
claim_supported: Distributed calibration can improve predictions; adequacy, identifiability and numerical stability remain relevant constraints.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 differentiable/adjoint modelling; P3 fair treatment of parameter heterogeneity.
limitations_or_caution: Counterexample to general rejection of complexity; not an independent test of our R2 specification.

authors: Müller Schmied, Hannes; Cáceres, Denise; Eisner, Stephanie; Flörke, Martina; Herbert, Claudia; Niemann, Christoph; Peiris, Thedini Asali; Popat, Eklavyya; Portmann, Felix Theodor; Reinecke, Robert; Schumacher, Maike; Shadkam, Somayeh; Telteu, Camelia-Eliza; Trautmann, Tim; Döll, Petra
title: The global water resources and use model WaterGAP v2.2d: model description and evaluation
hydrological_context: Groundwater, surface water, human water use and storages
method: WaterGAP hydrology, water-use models and net-abstraction coupling
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Surface-water and groundwater abstractions, storage and human water use affect water flows represented by large-scale hydrological models.
claim_supported: Surface-water and groundwater abstractions, storage and human water use affect water flows represented by large-scale hydrological models.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 motivate candidate non-routing components without attribution.
limitations_or_caution: Global model formulation is not evidence of local reservoir or irrigation activity; sign and magnitude may vary.
evidence_location: Abstract; reservoir and net-abstraction model descriptions

authors: Costelloe, J. F.; Peterson, T. J.; Halbert, K.; Western, A. W.; McDonnell, J. J.
title: Groundwater surface mapping informs sources of catchment baseflow
hydrological_context: Catchment baseflow with groundwater and ungauged tributaries
method: Groundwater-surface mapping, digital filtering and tracer mixing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Groundwater discharge contributes to baseflow, but hydrograph-based baseflow estimates need not identify groundwater or tributary sources uniquely.
claim_supported: Groundwater discharge contributes to baseflow, but hydrograph-based baseflow estimates need not identify groundwater or tributary sources uniquely.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 missing contribution and attribution ambiguity; avoid identifying a physical process from residual shape.
limitations_or_caution: Site-specific study; baseflow is not synonymous with groundwater and source separation has uncertainty.

authors: Saberi, Leila; McLaughlin, Rachel T.; Ng, G.-H. Crystal; La Frenierre, Jeff; Wickert, Andrew D.; Baraer, Michel; Zhi, Wei; Li, Li; Mark, Bryan G.
title: Multi-scale temporal variability in meltwater contributions in a tropical glacierized watershed
hydrological_context: Tropical glacierised watershed in Ecuador
method: Hydrochemical mixing, time-series analysis and integrated watershed model
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Meltwater, groundwater and streamflow relationships differ across timescales and pathways.
claim_supported: Meltwater, groundwater and streamflow relationships differ across timescales and pathways.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 physical plausibility of seasonal and delayed contributions.
limitations_or_caution: Different climatic region; neither raw temperature correlation nor Fourier seasonality establishes glacier causation here.

authors: Van Tiel, Marit; Van Loon, Anne F.; Seibert, Jan; Stahl, Kerstin
title: Hydrological response to warm and dry weather: do glaciers compensate?
hydrological_context: Glacier-fed catchments in Canada, Norway and the Alps
method: Warm/dry-event streamflow comparison against long-term regimes
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Glacier-fed catchments can respond to warm dry periods through meltwater and other storages, with compensation varying among catchments and events.
claim_supported: Glacier-fed catchments can respond to warm dry periods through meltwater and other storages, with compensation varying among catchments and events.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 discuss possible seasonal contributions and temperature dependence cautiously.
limitations_or_caution: Glacier cover and event conditions matter; no evidence for glacier dominance in this case.

authors: Wiersma, Pau; Aerts, Jerom; Zekollari, Harry; Hrachowitz, Markus; Drost, Niels; Huss, Matthias; Sutanudjaja, Edwin H.; Hut, Rolf
title: Coupling a global glacier model to a global hydrological model prevents underestimation of glacier runoff
hydrological_context: Large glacierised basins
method: GloGEM coupled with PCR-GLOBWB 2
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Explicit glacier dynamics and mass loss can change runoff estimates compared with a hydrological model with simplified glacier representation.
claim_supported: Explicit glacier dynamics and mass loss can change runoff estimates compared with a hydrological model with simplified glacier representation.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 demonstrate omitted source processes can alter simulated runoff.
limitations_or_caution: Model-based and glacier-specific; no inferred glacier contribution fraction at DSK.

authors: Nicolle, Pierre; Andréassian, Vazken; Royer-Gaspard, Paul; Perrin, Charles; Thirel, Guillaume; Coron, Laurent; Santos, Léonard
title: Technical note: RAT – a robustness assessment test for calibrated and uncalibrated hydrological models
hydrological_context: Hydrological models under changed climatic conditions
method: Robustness assessment test inspired by differential split-sample testing
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Temporal transferability and extrapolation require explicit assessment rather than reliance on calibration performance.
claim_supported: Temporal transferability and extrapolation require explicit assessment rather than reliance on calibration performance.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 generalisation caution and P4 fixed out-of-period evaluation.
limitations_or_caution: Climate-robustness assessment differs from our single-year holdout; neither certifies universal generalisation.

authors: Li, C. Z.; Zhang, L.; Wang, H.; Zhang, Y. Q.; Yu, F. L.; Yan, D. H.
title: The transferability of hydrological models under nonstationary climatic conditions
hydrological_context: Australian unimpaired catchments under climatic contrasts
method: Differential split-sample tests and parameter-stability assessment
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Calibration and evaluation under different climatic periods reveal context-dependent model transferability.
claim_supported: Calibration and evaluation under different climatic periods reveal context-dependent model transferability.
how_we_should_use_it: P3/P4 motivate cross-year stability and chronological holdout.
limitations_or_caution: Not proof that our short record samples climate extremes or satisfies a full differential split-sample protocol.

authors: Addor, Nans; Newman, Andrew J.; Mizukami, Naoki; Clark, Martyn P.
title: The CAMELS data set: catchment attributes and meteorology for large-sample studies
hydrological_context: US catchments minimally impacted by human activity
method: CAMELS meteorology, streamflow and catchment attributes
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Public large-sample data and documented attributes support comparative hydrology, with source limitations explicitly described.
claim_supported: Public large-sample data and documented attributes support comparative hydrology, with source limitations explicitly described.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 benchmarks and P4 transparency of data context.
limitations_or_caution: Dataset does not prescribe our chronological split or demonstrate leakage prevalence; minimally impacted basins limit direct transfer to regulated rivers.

authors: Klingler, Christoph; Schulz, Karsten; Herrnegger, Mathew
title: LamaH-CE: LArge-SaMple DAta for Hydrology and Environmental Sciences for Central Europe
hydrological_context: Central Europe; nested and intermediate catchments
method: LamaH-CE hourly/daily records, topology, quality and human-impact attributes
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Connected/intermediate catchments and documented quality and human-impact attributes enable network-aware comparative studies.
claim_supported: Connected/intermediate catchments and documented quality and human-impact attributes enable network-aware comparative studies.
how_we_should_use_it: P2 river benchmarks; P4 source quality and topology-aware evaluation.
limitations_or_caution: Connectivity can create shared information; dataset description itself does not prove leakage in other studies.

authors: Douglas Patton; Deron Smith; Muluken E Muche; Kurt Wolfe; Rajbir Parmar; John M Johnston
title: Catchment scale runoff time-series generation and validation using statistical models for the Continental United States
journal_or_venue: Environmental modelling & software : with environment data news
study_type: Statistical runoff modelling and evaluation study
hydrological_context: CONUS NHDPlus catchments; NLDAS-2 reference runoff
method: Three-part chronological splitting and spatial holdout
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Separating selection from final accuracy assessment and withholding time and space are used to avoid optimistically biased evaluation from leakage.
claim_supported: Separating selection from final accuracy assessment and withholding time and space are used to avoid optimistically biased evaluation from leakage.
how_we_should_use_it: P4 freeze-before-holdout rationale; state partition roles rather than copying labels.
limitations_or_caution: Authors call the selection partition test and final assessment validation; our labels differ. Reference runoff is modelled, not independent measured discharge.
evidence_location: Section 1.2 Model validation and selection; Figure 1

authors: Poudel, Sandeep; Steinschneider, Scott
title: An argument for parsimony in differentiable hydrologic models
hydrological_context: CAMELS-US HBV configurations
method: Static/dynamic and ensemble comparisons; feature replacement experiments
main_finding_relevant_to_this_paper: Similar predictive skill can coexist with different parameter interpretations; static features may function as proxies or identifiers rather than physical representations.
claim_supported: Similar predictive skill can coexist with different parameter interpretations; static features may function as proxies or identifiers rather than physical representations.
how_we_should_use_it: P3 limited support for capacity-versus-interpretation concern and proxy ambiguity.
limitations_or_caution: Static geographic/attribute proxies differ from our temporal temperature proxy; does not prove a general literature-wide diagnostic omission.
